digest.intro: A day of thresholds: systems inverting, cells reversing, networks closing.

items.title: The Hormuz Pressure Cooker
items.blurb: Iran claims three tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz as Qatar races to broker a nuclear deal before what analysts expect will be US-Israel airstrikes following their respective domestic elections. The window for diplomacy is narrow and closing — midterms are the clock.

items.title: The Largest Crypto Heist Ever Took 20 Minutes
items.blurb: Starting at 4pm ET on October 29, hackers drained $6.3 billion from Binance wallets spread across at least ten blockchains — Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana — in roughly 20 minutes, with preparation apparently beginning 36 hours earlier. Three crypto-tracing firms independently point to North Korea; if confirmed, this single theft would nearly double everything Pyongyang has stolen in crypto to date. About half the funds have been frozen; the rest may be unrecoverable.

items.title: Google's AI Search Earns Less — So They're Adding More Ads
items.blurb: Alphabet posted $128B in Q3 revenue but missed EPS badly — analysts expected $3.02, got $2.12 — and the stock dropped ~12%, one of the largest post-earnings falls in its history. The core problem: Google itself admitted AI-powered search generates less revenue than organic search, and their response is to stuff more ads into it while spending even more on AI next year. This is the economic stress fracture of the AI transition playing out in real time.

items.title: SpaceX Has Outgrown NASA
items.blurb: The Ars piece traces an institutional inversion that's now nearly complete: SpaceX spent years hacking through Boeing and Lockheed to win government contracts, and won so thoroughly that it has flipped from dependent contractor to indispensable infrastructure — and is now visibly losing interest in NASA as a customer outside of Starshield data services. Former NASA deputy administrator Lori Garver says she 'literally cannot wrap her head around' a future without Dragon and Falcon flying for the agency, but the signs are accumulating. Sovereign space capability is now a private company's side project.

items.title: Reddit Is Closing the Open Web's Last Big Commons
items.blurb: Steve Huffman confirmed in a shareholder letter that Reddit is moving to a logged-in-only experience, citing ad targeting, engagement, data corpus protection, and regulatory pressures — and noting search referral traffic dropped by over a million visits per week in October alone. The explicit goal is protecting 'extremely valuable corpus of data' from open crawling. The last major legible community archive is going behind a wall; what that does to training data, research access, and the open web is not a quarterly metrics story.

items.title: Backdoor in Claude Code VS Code Extension — Operational Alert
items.blurb: Phorion found a persistent SSH backdoor embedded in the official Claude Code for VS Code extension version 2.1.313 on the Cursor Marketplace — targeting macOS, Linux, and Windows, running with full IDE permissions on load, giving attackers immediate access to local files and source code. Cursor has pulled the release from its marketplace and associated NPM/VSCode registries. If you or anyone on your team used this version, treat it as a confirmed incident and review accordingly.

items.title: 54% of Early-Onset Diabetics Reached Drug-Free Remission in Six Months
items.source: ScienceDaily / The Lancet Regional Health Americas
items.blurb: A McGill/Leicester RCT published today in The Lancet found that 54% of adults under 45 with type 2 diabetes achieved full remission within six months on a structured low-calorie diet plus exercise program — versus 4% in the usual-care control group. Early-onset T2D is particularly aggressive, so the intervention window matters more here than in older-onset cases. This is a randomized controlled trial, not an observational study, which makes the effect size genuinely striking.

items.title: A Funeral for Dead Networks
items.blurb: In Amsterdam, participants arrived in funeral attire to write eulogies for AOL chat rooms, MSN Messenger, and other dead networks — not out of nostalgia, but as a deliberate act of media archaeology. The facilitator's argument is pointed: AOL chat rooms were not primitive Slack; they were specific places with specific people, and when they went, something socially real was lost that no successor inherited. Treating deprecation as an event worth grieving is framed explicitly as resistance to the consumerist logic that makes obsolescence feel natural and not worth mourning — a frame that cuts directly at today's Reddit story.

items.title: I'm So Bad at Billiards That I Ended Up in the Hyperbolic Plane
items.blurb: Mathematical billiards — tracing what happens to a ball bouncing in differently shaped tables — turns out to be a clean on-ramp into non-Euclidean geometry, specifically the hyperbolic plane, visualized with the care that makes abstract topology feel spatial and navigable. The HN math community flagged it as genuinely illuminating rather than just pretty. If you've ever worked with curved UV spaces or non-Euclidean rendering and wanted a geometric intuition that isn't purely algebraic, this is 15 minutes well spent.

facts.fact: The North Korea-linked Binance hack, if confirmed, would nearly double the total amount Pyongyang has ever stolen in cryptocurrency — from a single 20-minute operation.
Alphabet's Q3 earnings per share came in at $2.12 against analyst consensus of $3.02 — a miss of nearly a dollar per share that wiped roughly $500 billion in market value in a single day.
In the McGill/Leicester diabetes trial, only 4% of participants receiving standard care achieved remission — compared to 54% in the intensive lifestyle group, a 13.5× difference.
Reddit's logged-out search referral traffic dropped by more than one million visits per week during October 2026 alone — which is part of why the company is accelerating its move to a login wall.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A film that operates as an essay on memory, ritual, and the invisible systems that make cultures cohere — filmed observation as philosophy, structured like a feedback loop between Japan and Guinea-Bissau. The template for every earnest rabbit-hole essay since, and still the ceiling.

art_picks.title: Process and Program (paintings and objects)
art_picks.creator: Haegue Yang
art_picks.why: Yang's practice turns industrial materials — Venetian blinds, bells, dried vegetation — into multisensory systems that encode migration, East Asian cosmology, and the phenomenology of labor without ever explaining itself. Her current Dia Beacon commission 'Through' is the biggest argument for her work yet.

art_picks.title: Versions
art_picks.creator: Mark Fell
art_picks.why: Fell treats rhythm not as groove but as a system — modular synthesis exposed as pure decision-tree, beautiful in the way circuit diagrams are beautiful. The surface is cold and playful; the structure underneath is obsessively deep. Exactly the kind of thing that makes you want to open Max/MSP.

events.name: Pierre Huyghe: UUmwelt
events.venue: MoMA Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Sculpture Garden, 11 W 53rd St, Manhattan
events.why: Huyghe worked with Kyoto neuroscientists to fMRI-scan a human imagining images, then had a neural network reconstruct what was seen — the hallucinatory outputs play on freestanding screens in the Sculpture Garden, activated in real time by visitor gaze and cancer-cell mutation data; it's exactly the edge where biological systems, machine cognition, and public space collapse into one another.

events.name: Haegue Yang: Through
events.venue: Dia Beacon, 3 Beekman St, Beacon, NY
events.why: Yang's largest US commission takes over Dia Beacon's two levels with louver sculptures, bells, and color-coded cardinal axes drawn from the Five Phases philosophy — a translation of exiled Korean composer Isang Yun's music into physical space; the architecture becomes the instrument.

events.name: Salon Art + Design — 15th Edition
events.venue: Park Avenue Armory, 643 Park Ave, Manhattan
events.why: The serious collectible design fair — furniture, ceramics, lighting, and blue-chip 20th-century work from international galleries — where the category boundary between functional object and sculpture is the entire point; skip the mainstream art fairs and come here instead.

events.name: Art Week NYC — Inaugural Edition
events.venue: Citywide (New Museum anchor, 235 Bowery; hub in Midtown; galleries across Chelsea, Tribeca, LES, UES)
events.why: The first-ever citywide art week co-organized by Artforum, ARTnews, and the New Museum — 76+ galleries open simultaneously, plus a November 14 day of public talks at the New Museum titled 'Site Conditions: Five Talks on Art and the City' covering museum redesigns, AI in studio practice, and the economics of working in New York; worth going for the New Museum programming alone.

events.name: Doris Salcedo — New Exhibition
events.why: Salcedo makes sculpture out of violence and disappearance — furniture embedded in concrete, fabric sutured like wounds — one of the few artists who consistently transforms political catastrophe into form without aestheticizing it away.
